title: Cryosectioning, block face imaging and Nissl staining fluorescently labeled pig heart
protocol: Place the blank slides into a UV cross-linker.
Irradiate the slides at 220nm-260nm at full power for 30 minutes.
Place a flat metal tin in a bucket of dry ice prior to cryosectioning.
Remove the OCT-embedded tissue sample from the -80°C freezer and place into the cryostat 20-30 minutes before cryosectioning.
Mount and position a camera to the cryostat.
Acquire an image of the block face prior to each sectioning iteration.
Set the cryostat to a section thickness of 40 µm.
Mount each tissue section on the flat side of the frame slide, within the membrane window.
Support the frame membrane slide on a glass slide to reinforce the membrane during tissue mounting.
Immediately after mounting the tissue sections, place a clean gloved finger onto the “well” side of the slide for 2-3 seconds.
Transfer the slide (well side down) to a flat metal tin within a bucket of dry ice.
Store the slides in a labeled slide box at -80°C overnight or up to one month.
Prepare the staining solutions on the day of the staining procedure.
Mix 50 mL of 100% ethanol with 12.5 µl Superase-In RNase Inhibitor.
Keep the mixture at room temperature.
Mix 47.5 mL of 100% ethanol with 2.5 mL Molecular Grade Water and 12.5 µL Superase-In RNase Inhibitor.
Keep the mixture at room temperature.
Mix 50 mL of 1X PBS with 12.5 µl Superase-In RNase Inhibitor.
Keep the mixture at room temperature.
Mix 50 µL of 0.1% cresyl violet solution with 49.95 mL Molecular Grade Water and 12.5 µL Superase-In RNase Inhibitor to yield a 0.0001% cresyl violet solution.
Keep the light-sensitive mixture at room temperature.
Take the prepared 100% cold ethanol solution from the -20°C freezer.
Place the solution into a bucket containing regular ice.
Immerse frame slide containing tissue section in the 100% cold ethanol solution and let sit for 1 minute.
Remove the frame slide from the 100% cold ethanol solution, lay flat and gently pipette the 1X PBS solution onto the frame slide for approximately 1 minute without directly applying it on tissue.
Pipette 1X PBS solution on to frame slide and let sit for 30 seconds then continually pipette 1X PBS solution on to slide for another 30-45 seconds.
Tilt frame slide to pour off excess 1X PBS solution and replace Kimwipe.
Gently pipette the 0.0001% cresyl violet solution onto the frame slide ensuring the entire tissue section is immersed in the solution.
Pipette 0.0001% cresyl violet solution onto frame slide and let sit for 4 minutes.
Tilt frame slide to pour off excess cresyl violet stain and replace Kimwipe.
Gently pipette the 1X PBS solution on to the frame slide for 1 minute to wash away any excess cresyl violet stain.
Pipette 1X PBS solution onto frame slide continually for 1 minute.
Tilt frame slide to pour off excess 1X PBS solution and replace Kimwipe.
Pipette 95% ethanol solution on to the frame slide and let sit for 1 minute.
Tilt frame slide to pour off excess 95% ethanol solution and replace Kimwipe.
Pipette 100% ethanol solution onto the frame slide immersing the tissue for 1 minute.
Tilt frame slide to pour off excess 100% ethanol solution and immediately immerse entire frame slide into a xylene solution limiting air exposure.
Immerse frame slide in xylene solution and let sit for 1 minute.
Remove slide from xylene solution and let sit under fume hood for 15-20 minutes or until tissue section appears dry.
Mix cresyl violet stained neurons with excitation at 546/10 nm and emission at 580-590 nm.
Label neurons with Fast Blue and set excitation to 365 nm and emission to 420 nm.
